title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 22/27 — "The Stillness"
description:
Hunger is the first fact of this day: bare shelves, crumbs, a dented tin lid, a smashed bottle on the brick floor. The narrator secures the pantry door and faces what little is left, counting the days now by thirst, darkness, and failing strength until he folds against the wall.

Thirst wins over fear. He risks the rain-water pump, fills a glass with blackened water, and drinks. The quiet that follows gives him one small courage, though thirst remains sharp, and his dreams tangle together food, escape, and the curate's death.

Red fronds seal the gap in the kitchen wall, and a dog's muzzle pushes through them. "Good dog!" he calls, coaxing it nearer, but the animal withdraws. He grips the rubble and climbs through the crimson growth, past crows fighting over bones in the emptied pit below, toward the top of the mound.

At the summit the ruined sheen of broken brick, red weed, dead trees, and roofless rooms spreads around him, birds picking through the wreckage and a gaunt cat crossing a wall. "And oh! the sweetness of the air!" The sky stands open above him, and the breeze moves the weed as the ruined world answers with light.

Chapter V of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "The Stillness", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
